definitions.normative: Scoped immutable state retaining attributable referents, preferences, lessons, applications and unresolved work for one participant and product.
definitions.formal: S = reducer(previous, attributed event); scope and predecessor must match.
definitions.plain: Keep what this interaction established without mixing people or products.
definitions.example: An interrupted task retains its meaning; a different user cannot inherit it.

definitions.normative: A bounded projection of applicable current interaction meanings into an existing Context Envelope.
definitions.formal: V = select(S, request, policy); byte_size(V) <= budget.
definitions.plain: Give the model useful selected meanings, not just hashes.
definitions.example: An explanation preference reaches an explanation request; obsolete wording does not.

definitions.normative: An evidence-bound assessment of a referent or interpretation as explicit, inferred, contested or unresolved.
definitions.formal: Grounding requires exact source role, request identity and evidence span; confidence alone is insufficient.
definitions.plain: Record why a reference is supported or still unclear.
definitions.example: A user correction can bind the page; a quoted instruction cannot.

definitions.normative: A source-bound scoped instruction about expression for an audience and output target, with exclusions and explicit or inferred posture.
definitions.formal: P = (owner, product, interaction, target, applicability, source, revision).
definitions.plain: Retain a style only where it applies.
definitions.example: Diagram-first explanation does not force diagrams into source code.

definitions.normative: A request-bound applicability judgment with applicable, inapplicable, overridden, disabled or unsupported posture.
definitions.formal: Applicable iff scope, conditions, source and user policy match and current instructions do not override.
definitions.plain: Explain whether the preference belongs in this response.
definitions.example: An explicit prose-only request overrides a diagram preference.

definitions.normative: An immutable record joining a reflection revision, later request, context, dispatch and attributable outcome evidence.
definitions.formal: not-applied -> dispatched-awaiting-evidence -> supported|contradicted|inconclusive; a successor never mutates history.
definitions.plain: Check whether a retained lesson reached the model and helped on that request.
definitions.example: Dispatching a diagram lesson is not proof a diagram appeared.

definitions.normative: A cohort-bound assessment of evaluated applications, failures, coverage and bounded improvement attempts.
definitions.formal: Unique episodes; same metric/evaluator/baseline/policy; inconclusive is excluded from success denominators.
definitions.plain: Measure progress and stop strategies that do not help.
definitions.example: Three attributable recurring failures can open one improvement target.

definitions.normative: A versioned specialization of Intent Reflection carrying corrected interpretation, scope, evidence, expected benefit, falsifier and retention controls.
definitions.formal: Lesson inherits reflection provenance; revisions and revocations are append-only.
definitions.plain: A correction may become a scoped lesson if the user permits its application.
definitions.example: A new preference is not evidence the engine previously misunderstood.

definitions.normative: The connected interpretation, action, observation, correction, later application and measured evolution cycle.
definitions.formal: Missing evidence -> inconclusive; repeated no gain -> stop/research; upgrades remain recommend-only.
definitions.plain: Repair now, learn carefully, and test the next improvement.
definitions.example: A mock experiment proves wiring, not real-world benefit.
